test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: The amount of depreciation charged on a machinery item is debited to the depreciation account.
Depreciation means decrease in the value of an asset.
In the reducing balance method, the amount charged to depreciation declines.

solution:
The correct answer is** Depreciation is a cash item.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Depreciation is a cash item:**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. Depreciation is a non-cash expense. It represents the allocation of the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life and does not involve any actual cash outflow.
 
• Depreciation is recorded in the financial statements to match the cost of the asset with the revenue it generates, adhering to the matching principle in accounting.
 
• Being a non-cash item, depreciation impacts the net income but not the cash flow directly.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The amount of depreciation charged on a machinery item is debited to the depreciation account:**

 
 
• This statement is correct. The depreciation expense is debited to the depreciation account, which is an expense account, and credited to the accumulated depreciation account, which is a contra-asset account.
 
 
 
• **Depreciation means decrease in the value of an asset:**
 
 
• This statement is correct. Depreciation reflects the reduction in the value of an asset over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
 
 
 
• **In the reducing balance method, the amount charged to depreciation declines:**
 
 
• This statement is correct. In the reducing balance method (also known as the declining balance method), depreciation is calculated as a fixed percentage of the book value of the asset, which decreases each year. As a result, the depreciation expense declines over time.
